original.reason: It assumes a one-point compactification without addressing the compact case; under the standard construction this requires noncompactness. The argument is otherwise correct once that case is handled separately.

judgment.reason: For an arbitrary closed F in X, F need not be closed in the one-point compactification Y. Thus Urysohn's lemma cannot be applied to F and {x} as claimed.
Both cases are handled correctly: the noncompact one-point compactification is compact Hausdorff, hence completely regular, and complete regularity is hereditary.
It incorrectly asserts that every closed subset F of X is closed in the one-point compactification Y.
The compact and noncompact cases are correctly treated, using the hereditary nature of complete regularity.
